title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts, capture the trace store's returned execution id and expose
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts, capture the trace store's returned execution id and expose it on the compose report, so a compose run can be graded afterwards.

Today that emission is fire-and-forget. The single line in this file containing the text v2/activities/executions begins with `void fetch(`, so the response is discarded. That response body is `{ success: true, data: { execution_id: "..." } }`, and that id is the only address by which this execution can later be graded. Because it is thrown away, the reach verdict is addressed to a synthetic id that matches no stored row, and 894 of 899 compose executions are ungraded.

Make two coordinated changes, both in this one file.

First, declare `let traceExecutionId: string | null = null;` immediately before the `try {` that wraps that emission. Change that `void fetch(` into an awaited call whose JSON response is read, assigning `traceExecutionId` from `data.execution_id` when it is a non-empty string. The enclosing function is already async, so awaiting is safe. Preserve every existing guarantee exactly: keep `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`, keep the trailing `.catch(...)` and the outer `catch`, and leave `traceExecutionId` as null on any failure, so a trace-store hiccup can never fail or slow a compose.

Second, in the returned report body, immediately after the line beginning `restored_files: restored.map`, add the line `trace_execution_id: traceExecutionId,` so the captured id reaches the caller.

Both changes are required together: the variable without the report field would be unused code.

Change no other file.
